entities.name: Late Period of ancient Egypt
entities.label: Timeframe
entities.summary:
Late Period of ancient Egypt was a pivotal timeframe spanning from 663 BCE to 331 BCE, primarily associated with North Africa. This era marked a significant chapter in the development of human societies, with notable achievements such as the construction of the Great Library of Alexandria and the reign of the powerful pharaohs like Psamtek III and Nectanebo II.

The Late Period was characterized by the rise of the Hellenistic period in Egypt, with the conquest of Alexander the Great and the subsequent Ptolemaic dynasty. This period also saw the decline of the ancient Egyptian economy and the rise of foreign influences, such as the Greek and Persian empires.

The legacy of the Late Period can be seen in the many cultural and architectural achievements that continue to inspire wonder today, such as the temples of Edfu and Kom Ombo. The period also laid the groundwork for the Roman conquest of Egypt in 30 BCE, marking the end of the ancient Egyptian era.

The sheer magnitude of human societies' development during this period is encapsulated in the fact that the Late Period of ancient Egypt was documented across 51 language editions of Wikipedia.
